Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.
At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device.
We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
As a Senior Engineering Manager, Communications, you'll lead the team responsible for in-game text chat — one of the most-used surfaces on Roblox and a cornerstone of how our community connects. Every day this system carries billions of messages across hundreds of millions of users, in real time, across 2D and 3D spaces, on every device we support. You'll own the roadmap and the engineering org behind it: building rich, immersive, and engaging communication experiences that let people and creators express themselves safely and seamlessly — better than in real life.
This is a role for a leader who thinks like a product builder as much as an engineer. You'll balance the demands of massive scale and rock-solid reliability with a relentless focus on the user experience, shipping features that make conversation on Roblox feel effortless, expressive, and safe. You'll grow and develop a team of engineers, set technical direction, and partner deeply across product, design, trust & safety, and infrastructure to define what communication on Roblox becomes next.
You Will
Lead, grow, and develop a team of software engineers building the in-game text chat platform, setting a high bar for engineering excellence, ownership, and career growth.
Own the technical vision and multi-quarter roadmap for real-time text messaging, balancing new product capabilities against scale, latency, reliability, and cost.
Drive the architecture and evolution of messaging systems that reliably deliver billions of messages per day at low latency to a global, cross-platform audience.
Partner with product and design to shape a compelling communication experience — treating chat as a product, not just infrastructure — and translate ambiguous goals into concrete plans and shipped features.
Collaborate closely with Trust & Safety, Policy, and ML teams to ensure every messaging experience is safe and civil by design for a young, global user base.
Establish strong engineering practices around quality, observability, on-call health, and operational excellence for systems that must always be available.
Communicate clearly and influence across the organization — with peers, leadership, and cross-functional partners — to align teams behind a shared direction.
You Have
8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years managing and growing engineering teams.
A track record of building and shipping consumer-facing products at scale — ideally messaging, communications, social, or other real-time systems.
Strong product intuition: you make thoughtful tradeoffs between user experience, technical complexity, and speed, and you care about what you ship, not just how it's built.
Deep experience designing and operating large-scale distributed systems, with a strong grasp of reliability, latency, and the realities of running high-throughput services in production.
Demonstrated ability to attract, develop, and retain strong engineers, and to build healthy, high-performing teams.
Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills, with a history of driving alignment across product, design, and engineering.
A bias toward action and a comfort with ambiguity, especially at high scale.
You Might Also Have
Experience with real-time messaging protocols, presence systems, or high-fanout delivery infrastructure.
Background in trust & safety, content moderation, or safety-critical systems.
Experience building communication or social features for large, global, or youth audiences.
Familiarity with cross-platform (mobile, console, desktop) product development.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
We're looking for experienced engineers to build Anthropic's cache layer as a managed service from the ground up. The Caching team is part of the Databases organization and owns the systems that keep Anthropic's hottest paths fast and correct: a managed Redis fleet, client libraries used across the company, and CDC-driven cache invalidation that solves one of distributed systems' hardest problems the right way.
This is a foundational role on a small team with outsized leverage. Every millisecond you take off a hot path is multiplied across every Claude request. You'll set the technical direction for caching at Anthropic, from the data plane to the developer experience, and you'll work closely with product and research teams to make caching something engineers get for free rather than something they have to think about.
Key responsibilities
Drive the technical direction for caching infrastructure used across Product and Research
Design, build, and operate a managed Redis fleet that scales to support millions of users across Claude's product ecosystem
Build client libraries and developer-facing abstractions that make correct caching the default for Anthropic engineers
Design and operate CDC-driven cache invalidation that keeps cached data consistent with source-of-truth databases
Architect caching solutions that operate across GCP, AWS, first-party deployments, and other environments
Optimize latency, hit rates, reliability, and cost efficiency on Anthropic's hottest paths
Build observability and tooling that makes cache behavior easy to understand and debug
Partner with product and research teams to understand access patterns and build infrastructure that accelerates their work
Make build-vs-buy decisions for caching technologies
Minimum qualifications
Significant experience as a software engineer building and operating production distributed systems
Deep knowledge of caching architectures, including invalidation strategies, consistency tradeoffs, and failure modes
Experience operating Redis, Memcached, or similar in-memory data stores in production
Proficiency in at least one systems programming language (e.g., Go, Rust, Java, C++) or Python at scale
Track record of leading large, complex infrastructure projects as an engineer or tech lead
Ability to balance moving quickly with the reliability needs of production systems
Strong technical leadership and cross-functional collaboration skills
Preferred qualifications
10+ years building and scaling distributed infrastructure, with 3+ years leading large-scale projects or teams
Experience building managed infrastructure platforms or internal services consumed by many engineering teams
Experience with change data capture (Debezium or similar) or streaming data infrastructure
Experience operating Redis Cluster, Valkey, ElastiCache, Memorystore, or similar managed offerings at scale
Experience designing client libraries or SDKs for internal infrastructure
Experience scaling infrastructure through periods of rapid growth at high-growth companies
Experience with multi-cloud or hybrid cloud deployments
Contributions to caching systems, database internals, or related open source projects
Note: Prior AI/ML infrastructure experience is not required. We value deep infrastructure expertise from any domain.

jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Are you the kind of person who makes complex things work smoothly? The person who walks into a room of competing priorities and finds the path forward? Who builds trust across teams, champions safety without being asked and leaves every environment a little more capable than they found it? If that sounds like you, keep reading. What you'll actually be doing and why it matters At Bristol Myers Squibb , the medicines we make change lives. And behind every batch, every stability study, every regulatory submission, there's a GMP laboratory environment that has to be safe, ready, and performing at its best - every single day. That's where you come in. As our GMP Laboratory Operations Lead for Building 6 , will sit at the heart of our Moreton site's Analytical Science and Operations team - connecting three distinct laboratory organisations (Analytical Leadership & Testing, Long Term Stability, and Marketed Life Stability) into a cohesive, high-performing whole. You'll be the person who makes sure the right conversations happen at the right time, that resources are aligned before they become a problem, that safety is embedded in the culture - not just the paperwork - and that when an auditor walks through our doors, we're more than ready to welcome them. This is a role where your impact is visible, broad, and lasting. Here's what a typical week might look like You're facilitating the Building 6 Laboratory Leadership Team - bringing ALT, LTS and MLS together to align on priorities, navigate competing demands, and make joined-up decisions that keep the labs moving forward You're working alongside GMP Laboratory Systems to make sure equipment qualification, calibration and maintenance activities are planned around operational needs - not in spite of them You're delivering hands-on training on a new analytical technique to a scientist who's just picked it up, making sure it sticks rather than being a one-off demo You're coaching an early-career scientist who's just taken on their first safety rep role, helping them find their voice and build their confidence You're leading a cross-functional discussion on lessons learned from a recent near-miss - turning it into a genuine improvement, not just a tick-box exercise You're preparing your teams for an upcoming regulatory inspection - not in a scramble, but calmly, because you've built a culture of readiness No two days are the same. And that's exactly the point. What you'll gain from this role Real influence, without needing a title to back it up. This role is built around matrix leadership - which means you'll develop and demonstrate one of the most valued skills in modern organisations: the ability to bring people with you through trust, clarity and collaboration rather than hierarchy. Breadth that builds your career. You'll work across laboratory operations, EHS, quality, capability development, infrastructure and strategic planning. That kind of cross-functional exposure is rare and it positions you brilliantly for senior leadership roles in science, operations or quality. A community, not just a job. You'll be the cultural anchor for the Building 6 laboratory community. You'll mentor apprentices and graduates, champion emerging scientists and leaders and actively shape the kind of environment people want to come to work in. That legacy matters - to them, and to you. A seat at the table where it counts. When the site faces its biggest operational challenges - resource pressure, regulatory scrutiny, infrastructure change - you'll be in the room. You won't be waiting to hear what was decided; you'll be part of making the decision. Visible impact on patient outcomes. Everything you do - keeping labs audit-ready, driving continuous improvement, building safety culture - directly enables the science that gets medicines to patients. That connection is real and it's something you'll feel every day. What you'll bring You don't need to have done this exact role before but you do need to bring: Solid GMP laboratory experience - you understand the regulated environment deeply and you've operated within it successfully A track record of working across complex, matrixed organisations - you know how to navigate ambiguity and align stakeholders without it becoming exhausting for everyone involved A genuine passion for safety - not as a compliance obligation but as something you personally believe in and actively promote The ability to influence without authority - people follow your lead because you earn it, not because an org chart says so Experience driving change and improvement - you've seen what good looks like and you know how to take others on the journey with you A scientific degree or equivalent hands-on experience - the credibility to be taken seriously in a highly technical environment The bigger picture BMS is on a mission to transform patients' lives through science. Our Moreton site is a critical part of that mission and Building 6 is at the heart of how we maintain the quality and safety standards that make it possible. This role isn't just about keeping the lights on. It's about building something - a laboratory community that's safer, more capable, more connected, and more ready for the future than it was before you arrived. If you're ready to lead with influence, develop with purpose, and make a tangible difference to the people around you and the patients we ultimately serve - we'd love to hear from you. #LI-Hybrid We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. jobs.description: We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own and define the technology portfolio that powers our Omnichannel and Expert growth.
